newsitem.title: UK: Second VLCC of Iraqi crude set for South Africa.
newsitem.headline: Second VLCC of Iraqi crude set for South Africa.

text.p: A second shipment of Iraqi crude oil is due to leave for South Africa at the end of March under the United Nations oil-for-food deal, oil traders and shipping sources said on Wednesday.
British Petroleum (BP) has fixed the 276,000 tonne Athos to load about two million barrels of Basrah Light crude at Iraq's Gulf Mina al Bakr terminal on March 26.
BP has a term contract with Iraq's State Oil Marketing Organisation (SOMO) to lift 10,000 bpd over six months and a spot contract for 1.9 million barrels.
The crude will be processed at the 160,000 bpd Durban refinery -- a BP/Shell joint venture.
Last month, the U.N. agreed a pricing formula for Iraqi exports to South Africa of Dated Brent less $2.15 a barrel fob Mina al Bakr for cargoes loading in March.
On February 20, the Leonidas, carrying about two million barrels of Basrah Light, arrived in South Africa's Saldanha Bay after 63 days at sea.
The oil was originally destined for Mobil Corp in the U.S. Gulf but a delay caused by engine trouble in the Atlantic prompted Mobil to cancel its purchase.
The cargo was eventually sold to Caltex, a joint venture between Chevron and Texaco, for refining at its Cape Town plant.
